fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (30.5x x FY28E EPS $10.40 = $317, weight 0.45), FCF yield (FY28E FCF/share ~$9.80 at a 3.1% yield, reflecting a 5.2% 10-year yield less a growth premium = $316, weight 0.35) and the probability-weighted scenario value ($334, weight 0.20). The result is ~$320, about 6% below spot.

methods.name: Forward P/E
methods.detail: By Sep-2027 the market prices FY28 EPS. FY26 ~$8.86 (9M $6.88 + ~$1.98 FQ4, incl. ~$0.11 one-off tariff refund), FY27 consensus ~$9.58 (+8%), FY28 haircut to $10.40 for memory at ~$2.00/Gb through at least H1 2028 and a possible China chip tariff from 2027-06-23. Multiple 30.5x: above the ~27-29x five-year average for services mix and buybacks, well below today's ~35.6x FY27 given a Fed hiking cycle (3.75-4.00%) and a 5.18% 10-year yield.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.detail: FY28E FCF ~$140B on ~14.3B diluted shares (~2.5%/yr buyback shrink) = ~$9.80/share; required FCF yield 3.1% (5.2% risk-free less ~2pt for durable mid/high-single-digit growth and net-cash-neutral capital return) = ~$316.

methods.name: Scenario-weighted
methods.detail: 0.27 x $250 + 0.50 x $338 + 0.23 x $425 = ~$334; includes momentum/buyback drift that the static multiples ignore.

bear.story: Memory contracted ~33% higher for 2027 with the supply gap widening (-13.6%) keeps gross margin pinned at or below ~46%. Price hikes dent iPhone 18/Duo units, especially in China. A punitive China chip-tariff rate lands on 2027-06-23, and the Fed keeps hiking with the 10-year above 5%. FY28 EPS ~$9.3 and the multiple derates to ~27x.

base.story: iPhone 18/Duo pricing broadly offsets memory costs, and margin holds ~46-47% through price rather than cost relief. Services grow ~11-12% once the FX drag fades, the Google payment stays intact pending appeal, and buybacks continue. FY28 EPS ~$10.4 while the multiple compresses from ~36x toward ~32-33x under 5% yields, leaving the stock roughly flat plus the dividend.

bull.story: Gemini-based Siri and the foldable Duo drive a real upgrade supercycle. Pricing power beats memory inflation (margin ~47-48% despite no cost relief), services reaccelerate as FX flips, and yields ease. FY28 EPS ~$11.2 at ~38x.

thesis_break_reason: About -27% from $341, just above the 52-week low of $243 and ~26x FY27 consensus of $9.58. With the 10-year at 5.18% and the Fed hiking, a rate-driven de-rating to ~27-28x on unchanged estimates could by itself take the stock to the high $250s-$260s, so I lowered the break from $255. A close below ~$250 would most likely mean estimates are being cut: gross margin guided well below 46% because $2/Gb memory outruns price increases, iPhone unit declines after price hikes, a punitive China chip-tariff rate in June 2027, or an appellate ruling that bars the Google payments.

reasoning: The supervisor's fact-check confirmed my main round-1 calls. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and the 10-year closed at 5.18% on the as-of date (CNBC also reported 5.06-5.14% highs, the first since 2007). Memory is contracted ~33% higher for 2027, the CFO attributed more than 100% of the sequential GM drop to memory, and FY26 EPS is ~$8.86, so FY27 growth is only ~8%. I therefore keep a below-spot fair value. Three findings moved me. (1) The Services slowdown is mostly FX (~5pt drag, guided similar ex-FX), so I raised base-case services growth and nudged the P/E multiple from 30x to 30.5x. (2) The Google payment is not barred by current remedies. Oral argument is unscheduled (Google's reply brief is due 2026-09-29) and a ruling is likely mid-to-late 2027, so I removed it from the base case and kept it as a late-horizon tail. (3) The China chip tariff steps up on 2027-06-23 at a rate still to be set, which I missed. I added it as a bear driver and catalyst, and it lowers FY28 margin upside. On net the bull case loses 2pts of probability and the bear case gains 2pts. I added an FCF-yield method tied explicitly to the 5.2% risk-free rate ($316) and blended it with P/E ($317) and scenarios ($334) to get $320 (was $312). As in round 1, momentum, buybacks and product-cycle strength (record close on 2026-09-25) keep the median near spot rather than at fair value, and I trimmed it to ~$337, giving P(>=341)=0.48 (was 0.485). Dispersion is a ~27% lognormal (25% realized, bumped for rate and memory event risk) with a fattened left tail for abrupt de-rating and the June-2027 tariff event. The 10-90% range is roughly $237-$445. I lowered the thesis break from $255 to $250 because rate-driven de-rating alone can reach the high $250s.
